specification.title: Runner B starts while runner A is inside the migration
steps: The runner holds advisory lock K on its own session.
Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts its marker, then waits on select pg_advisory_xact_lock(K), inside the migration's transaction.
Checkpoint inside-A: A's session is waiting for K.
Runner B applies { m1 }. For the bound, B may exit, reach the gate, or stay blocked on the framework's own coordination.
Release K. A and B finish within the deadline. Runner C applies { m1 }.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the last runner has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: After every runner has finished, the migration's marker count is 1 and history holds one entry for it.
A runner that did not apply the migration either waited and then found it applied, or reported failure (non-zero exit status).
No runner starts executing the migration while another runner's execution of it is still live (its session still inside the migration): two live sessions inside it at once is a violation.

execution.description: Database.BeginTransactionAsync, CommitAsync, and RollbackAsync. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. The native TX-01A violation is SaveChangesAsync, which EF Core wraps in a savepoint. Nested scopes use CreateSavepointAsync. Pooling is false. EnableRetryOnFailure is not called. The provider's default execution strategy is left in place.

configuration.writes: Database.ExecuteSqlAsync for markers; SaveChangesAsync for the native TX-01A unique violation
configuration.savepoints: CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, ReleaseSavepointAsync; SaveChangesAsync may create its own savepoint
configuration.execution_strategy: the provider default; EnableRetryOnFailure is not called

execution.form: Database.MigrateAsync on a Migration whose Up inserts the marker and optionally waits on the case gate. Down deletes the marker, refuses when ppcs.reversal is none, or raises after the delete when the reversal is partial-then-error.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: A runner that waits learns that another run is in progress. It does not learn, from a successful return alone, that its own execution was the one that committed.

api_outcome.basis: Database.MigrateAsync returned and EF logged that it was applying the migration
api_outcome.contract: EF Core 10 Database.MigrateAsync applies pending migrations compiled in this assembly, or moves to a target migration. On PostgreSQL the relational provider runs each migration in a transaction when the provider reports transactional migrations. This adapter does not take an advisory lock of its own before reading history. The migration SQL inserts the marker and, when the case holds the gate, waits on pg_advisory_xact_lock inside that migration. History is the table ef_migrations_history. The adapter reports applied when EF logs Applying migration, and nothing_to_do when MigrateAsync returns without that log. MigrateAsync("0") runs the Down method. An exception whose message says the migration has no reversal is reported as refused. Any other exception is reported as failed.
